method: Built-in image_gen; generated PNGs copied unchanged. Native alpha. No programmatic image edits.

assets.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the supplied dungeon modular sprite atlas. Keep the exact canvas, coordinates, widths, layout and complete outer silhouettes of every module. Transparent RGBA background.
Correct wall perspective and the protruding ledge effect. These are stone WALL TOPS, not steps or projecting cornices. For all vertically oriented stones and the vertical arms of the four L corners, paint over EVERY dark south-facing foot/band with the same light slate-blue TOP surface so each vertical run is a single flat horizontal plane with thin joints. Keep their full height, DO NOT shorten/remove their bottom ends. No upright front faces on vertical runs.
For the two horizontal three-stone strips and horizontal arms of corners: remove the thick dark projecting lower lip and its black undercut. Extend the soft blue upper plane to almost the bottom of the existing silhouette, leaving only a very narrow understated bevel, approximately 3 pixels, with a straight flush lower edge. These will sit directly above separately drawn dark masonry, with no overhang or ledge. Retain the same full silhouette footprint to preserve module joins.
Keep the blue hand-painted cartoon art and thin outlines, but quiet the white edge highlights, no new cracks, no checkerboard, no text. Do not move or resize any module; center large slab may stay unchanged. True native transparency around each complete sprite.

Use case: precise-object-edit. The supplied transparent atlas is the edit target. Keep the exact canvas and module registration. Change ONLY the two vertical TWO-STONE strips in middle-left and middle-right. They must read as two FLAT TOP-VIEW stone pavers in one plane, no steps. Repaint ALL dark bottom/front faces, including the large dark band at the bottom of the lower stone, as continuation of the light slate-blue TOP surface. Keep the full painted extents and heights; fill the dark bands with the top material rather than shortening sprites. No thick lower lip, no vertical fascia, no shadows cast beneath a stone; use only a thin 2–3-pixel joint/edge all around, quiet highlights. Keep the existing widths, positions, sizes and two-stone separation. Soften the busy diagonal surface texture. Other atlas elements unchanged. Transparent RGBA background, native alpha, no text, no checkerboard.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create a reusable game asset sheet of TWELVE INDIVIDUAL floor stone sprites, using the supplied floor image only as an art reference. Match its understated soft slate-blue/purple-gray dungeon floor, rounded lightly uneven edges, gentle painted patches and restrained narrow blue rim. The recent heavily crosshatched texture, identical repeated cracks and engraved diamond are unwanted. No diagonal crosshatch, no busy facets, no gritty speckles, no symbols. Keep cracks on some stones: bottom two rows each have a DIFFERENT restrained fracture pattern (off-center fork, fine diagonal, short corner crack, vertical meander, two small edge cracks, curved side crack). Six upper-row stones are calmer, with only soft wear or tiny nicks. Each stone has a quiet smooth painterly surface. Subtle per-stone color differences between muted blue, gray-blue and subdued purple-blue, similar brightness to reference.
Atlas precisely organized in 4 rows and 3 columns on a 1536 x 1536 transparent canvas. All twelve stones are separate COMPLETE silhouettes with generous transparent gutters, never touching. Each row: LEFT a narrow slab about 240px wide x256px tall; CENTER a medium slab 320x256; RIGHT a wide slab400x256. All heights identical. Rows are four color/wear/crack variants of these same three proportions. Rectangular near top view like reference with only thin edges, NO thick bottom front face. Uniform lighting from upper left. Keep full silhouettes inside their slots, no props, no background, no text or labels. True transparent alpha.
